note:
ISO 2026-W44 runs from October 26 through November 1. Uranus is about 4.9° in ecliptic longitude from Aldebaran in Taurus.

**Naked eye:** 🌕 Full Moon · Hunter's Moon — 04:11:49 UTC. Bright moonlight favors prominent stars and planets while reducing contrast on faint deep-sky objects. Use Scheat, Markab as the week’s fixed-sky framework.

**Planets:** Moon: Naked eye; magnitude -12.7; direct motion; 99.8% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Opposition in ecliptic longitude Oct 26 04:11 UTC. Conjunction with Ceres in ecliptic longitude Oct 31 15:27 UTC. Conjunction with Uranus in ecliptic longitude Oct 28 08:52 UTC. Mercury: In solar glare; magnitude 0.7; retrograde motion; 24.4% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Venus: In solar glare; magnitude -4.2; retrograde motion; 0.7% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Mars: Naked eye; magnitude 0.9; direct motion; 89.6% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Ceres: Telescope; magnitude 8.3; direct motion; 96.5% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Moon in ecliptic longitude Oct 31 15:27 UTC. Jupiter: Naked eye; magnitude -2.0; direct motion; 99.2% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Saturn: Naked eye; magnitude 0.4; retrograde motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Uranus: Binoculars; magnitude 5.6; retrograde motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Moon in ecliptic longitude Oct 28 08:52 UTC. Neptune: Telescope; magnitude 7.7; retrograde motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Pluto: Substantial telescope; magnitude 14.6; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot.

**Binoculars:** Trace Pisces’s charted figure in the finder, then identify Fumalsamakah at its charted position.

**Small telescope:** NGC 7479: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; Bubble Nebula: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; M52: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; Blue Snowball: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance

**Substantial telescope:** No fixed-sky Calendar object is classified as requiring a substantial telescope this week.

descriptors.name: Full Moon
descriptors.summary: Astronomical lunar phase near opposition to the Sun.
descriptors.body: Full Moon is the lunar phase in which the Moon and Sun are approximately opposite in geocentric ecliptic longitude, so the lunar disk is fully illuminated as seen from Earth.

story_candidates.dek: Scheat is a star in Pegasus of catalogue visual magnitude 2.44; its declination determines which latitudes can observe it.
story_candidates.body:
The stored catalogue gives a visual magnitude of 2.44. This is a catalogue value, not a prediction of its brightness this week. Lower magnitudes mean brighter objects; sky brightness and altitude affect whether you can see the star.

Its catalogue position is approximately right ascension 23h 03m and declination +28.1°. These reference coordinates describe its sky location; they are not an observing time or a current altitude.

At the almanac’s default latitude of 45° N, this star rises and sets, reaching approximately 73° altitude at upper culmination. These are geometric calculations from declination, excluding refraction and local obstructions. Darkness and the time of culmination must still be checked for the observing date and your location.

How to find it: Trace the preserved Pegasus stick figure from its brighter labeled stars, then identify the target on the corresponding charted segment.

Sources: Star Almanack’s stored fixed-object and expanded Bayer catalogues; accepted constellation figures and guiding-star routes. Visibility limits are original geometric calculations from catalogue declination, not weekly predictions.
